beats.caption: Good evening. We interrupt your scrolling with a story so big it needed its own feed.

data.headline: Local engineer replaces his resume with a feed of cartoon reels
data.ticker: Recruiters advised to keep scrolling  •  Marge demands royalties  •  PDF resume still available for traditionalists  •  More at eleven

beats.caption: Sources confirm: no bullet points. Just a tortoise, a cat and a man with a microphone.
Nobody remembers a resume. People remember things they scrolled.
He made his career SCROLLABLE, folks. Experts are calling it: content.
Back to you, Reginald. Reginald? He's asleep. Classic Reginald.

comments.text: I was not asleep. I was observing. Quietly.
In my day a resume was one page and it did not talk back.
the ticker is giving ✨production value✨

beats.caption: Here, in the corridors of a Pune university, we find a rare creature.
The young engineer has noticed something missing. A place for builders to gather.
So he does what few of his kind attempt. He builds the community himself, from nothing.
Two hundred members. Events of fifty to a hundred. An annual hackathon. Sponsored by GitHub itself.
His title: GitHub Campus Expert. The first and only one his university has ever had.

comments.text: TWO HUNDRED MEMBERS?? That's a stadium, Reggie!
It is not a stadium, Blaze. It is a WhatsApp group.
Did anyone bring snacks to these gatherings. Asking for myself.

beats.caption: Ladies and gentlemen, let's go to the numbers.

data.label: on this entire website
data.after: A feed, five characters and a talking cat

beats.caption: ZERO. Not one bullet point. Recruiters are reportedly sitting down.
The bullet points are still in the PDF. For emergencies.
Keep scrolling, folks. That's the whole resume now.

comments.text: I am the talking cat. I would like it noted.
A bold adaptation. The bullet point, extinct in the wild.
no bullet points is a whole personality

beats.caption: Leaving a review for Saurav.
Explains technical problems to people who don't read code. Calmly. Every day.
Very polite. Answers emails. Suspiciously organised.
Made a whole website about himself starring cartoon animals. Including me. Unpaid.
Three and a half stars. Half a star off for the unpaid part.

comments.text: THREE AND A HALF is Marge's HIGHEST SCORE EVER
It is not. I gave a radiator four once.
I'll take it.

beats.caption: Today's myth. One I hear far too often.

data.myth: You need a referral to land your first internship.
data.fact: Saurav cold-emailed his way into his first one. The audacity.

beats.caption: No connections. No referral. Just a polite, specific email to the right person.
Write to people. Most of them answer. Some of them even hire you.

comments.text: cold emailing is literally just sliding into DMs for LinkedIn people
Bold behaviour for a young engineer. I approve.

beats.caption: Okay so listen. Saurav's dad runs a sheet-metal company. Three plants.
They need new buyers. Like, actual factories that buy metal parts.
So instead of cold calling, he builds a whole automated outreach pipeline. Himself. On weekends.
AI finds the companies, scores them, writes the emails. Perfect, right? Right??

comments.text: I'm on the edge of my seat and I'm not even sitting
AI wrote the emails. I can already see where this is going.

beats.caption: Okay so. The AI scores and the AI emails? Wrong. A lot.
He spent his evenings cleaning up after the AI. Checking everything by hand.
Final count: 126 contacts in the CRM. One real reply, handed to the business head.
And the lesson became his next project: test the AI before you trust it. It's called Daedalus. Iconic.

comments.text: Told you. Check everything.
A healthy scepticism. Rare, and valuable.
part 3 when daedalus ships?? 👀

beats.caption: Tonight's guest is a software engineer who talks to business people. On purpose.
Every day I explain incidents and fixes to people who don't read code. Turns out I like that part.
He LIKES the meetings, folks!
I like where the tech meets the actual problem. That's the job I want.
Saurav, everybody! Engineer by day, translator by... also day!

comments.text: Someone who enjoys meetings. Unsettling.
the host is giving late-night energy fr
A rare hybrid. Observe it while you can.

beats.caption: I've been asked to rank Saurav's tools. Against my will.
Java. Old, reliable, never surprises anyone. Like me. S.
Azure. Certified in it twice. Overachiever. A.
React. Changes its mind every year. B.
AI engineering. Ask me again when Daedalus ships. C, for now.

comments.text: JAVA IN S TIER?? Marge has SPOKEN
react in B tier?? i'm shaking
Fair, honestly.

beats.caption: Local engineer replaces his resume with a feed of cartoon reels!
This man calls a website news.
In my day you printed your resume and nobody read it. Progress.
Still. The website is nice. Don't tell him I said that.

comments.text: MARGE STITCHED ME. I'M FRAMING THIS
stitch of the year honestly
A rare exchange between species.

beats.caption: Week one. He's already automated the manual job everyone hated.
Week two. Deploys that took hours now take minutes.
Week three. The incident report is written so clearly that even sales read it.
Month one. You're wondering why you didn't hire him sooner.

comments.text: Suspiciously organised. As I said.
WHERE DO I SIGN UP TO HIRE HIM
The manual job had it coming.

beats.caption: The creature wakes. Before food, before light, he speaks Spanish to an owl.
By day he works with herds in the United States and Europe. Briefly in sync. Mostly.
Then a few rounds of mental maths. The streak must survive.
Work ends. Work begins. He builds an AI that finds buyers for factories.
A chapter before sleep. Then, finally, rest. Briefly.

comments.text: Spanish before breakfast. Unnatural.
the work ends work begins is so real
HE NEVER STOPS, FOLKS. HE NEVER STOPS.
